You hear a lot of talk that the larger, more successful economies in the Eurozone (i.e., Germany) are lifting up the smaller and less successful nations (e.g. Greece). If you listen to critics of the Euro in places like Britain or Norway, they always argue against their nations joining the Euro, because then their economic strength would be stimied by events in Greece. If this is the case, why is Germany often seen as one of the great supporters of the Euro? Why don't they just return to the Mark and let Europe deal with their own problems?
ELI5: If Germany is carrying the rest of the Eurozone, and nations like Greece are dragging them back, why is Germany such a strong supporter of the Euro?

Most of Germany's exports are to other EU members and Germany has some of the highest exports in the EU. Other EU members use the same currency as Germany; the Euro. This is is important. If all European nations had their own currencies Germany's currency would be worth much more than a countries like Greece's due to its strong economy, making its exports much more expensive for other countries in the EU to import. If this happens people will import cheaper products not from Germany. With the Euro Germany can export a lot with minimal effect on the Euro's value, preserving the viability of cheap German exports. If Greece, Portugal and Spain were to leave the EU it would make their respective currencies dirt cheap compared to the Euro, making their exports much cheaper than Germany.

Germany is attempting to keep economic dominance of the Eurozone through keeping it together because they want to maintain their large amount of exports to their neighbors.

Germany is a manufacturing power house and a large percentage of their economy is based on exports, locking exchange rates (or using the same currency) benefits exporters.

Country A exports more to country B than the import from country B. As a result country A winds up with some of B's currency which they have to exchange. This exchange drives down the value of B's currency relative to A's currency. B's new lower valued currency makes their goods cheaper to purchasers in A, which increases exports to A. A's higher currency makes their goods more expensive to people in B which decreases exports to B. As a result the trade should balance. This can't happen if they both use the same currency so A can keep exporting more than they import every year making them very wealthy.

There are a lot of other ways to manipulate currency which break this simplified model, that is why you see perpetual trade deficits in other places (US-China for example) but that is another discussion all together.
